host.clocks: jetson_clocks applied 2026-10-15 (all 14 CPUs 2601 MHz, CPU idle states off, EMC 4266 MHz, nvpmodel 120W); verified before each batch from /sys and recorded in the batch host.json
host.note: taskset pinning of the processes the runner starts; other host processes are not isolated (no isolcpus). Remote desktop disconnected during batches.

purpose: P2 step 4 exploration (new batch after data/p2-20261015-batch-explore stopped on an abort-induced output-chain bracketing error): raise speed 1.5 -> 2.0 -> 2.5 -> 3.0 m/s with C->N N0 x3 and RAPTOR own-brake baseline x2 per level; stop escalating at the first level with a pre-registered flight failure; N->C C0 x3 at the highest level; best step-1 treatment (N2) x3 at the failed level. Flight failures are results; infrastructure failures stop.

output_chain_gate.basis: Recorded engineering acceptance agreement: 4 ms physics step, 12 ms maximum. The 12.5 ms rotor time constant is context, not proof of policy delay tolerance or stability.

failure_criteria.safety_envelope: any of tilt >= 45 deg, angular-rate component >= 8 rad/s, horizontal radius >= 10 m, altitude >= 8 m (frozen safety envelope; reaching the limit counts), or a runner safety abort
failure_criteria.no_joint_recovery: joint recovery not SETTLED within 10 s after the actual change (frozen P0 thresholds, active controller target)
failure_criteria.motor_saturation: any motor at >=0.999 or <=0.001 continuously for at least 0.5 s inside [trigger, window end]

rule: Flight failures (criteria above, with all infrastructure checks passing) are results and do not stop the batch; escalation stops after the first level with a flight failure. Infrastructure failures (PX4 exit, crash markers, readiness/DDS, trace or output-chain measurement or gate, metrics) stop the batch as usual.
escalation: Levels in order; after a level with any flight failure, or after the last level, run at_highest_level at that level; if that level had a flight failure also run at_failed_level there; then stop.
